analysis.title: Multi-Asset Strategy Daily
key_insights: The Fed delivered the expected skip, but the guidance was less hawkish than the market had priced. 2Y UST yields had pushed toward 4.78% before the meeting, with 2s10s briefly through 24bp, then reversed after Warsh's press conference. Warsh's acknowledgement that tighter financial conditions suggest policy is working pulled the front end lower and sent 2s10s back toward 34bp.

About 21bp of tightening is priced for December. Mizuho advises against extrapolating the post-FOMC rally too far, since the Fed did little to challenge a December hike. The open question is the pace of tightening in 2027.

Today's data is the focus: September PCE and the first Q3 GDP estimate. Mizuho's US senior economist sees room for an upside GDP surprise. Strong activity plus inflation would make it hard for USTs to extend the rally, particularly with $44bn of 7Y UST supply later in the day.
Mizuho would fade a month-end-led UST rally unless equities weaken more materially.
Tech is a rates input. Amazon reports tonight after Alphabet's miss revived some of the recent AI concerns.

Oil is offering some relief overnight after reports that JD Vance reached out to Iran to explore renewed talks, which took some geopolitical premium out of crude. Military action remains on the table after the midterms. Brent is around $114.75 per barrel, still broadly rangebound.

The ECB is expected to hold rates today, so the debate is about December. A December hike is still heavily priced. Lagarde must balance an inflation picture complicated by higher energy prices against a clear tightening in financial conditions. Mizuho expects her to keep meeting-by-meeting language with a tightening bias, and emphasis on tighter financial conditions could test December pricing.
The Bank Lending Survey showed another tightening in credit standards, and higher outright yields and wider EGB spreads are already doing part of the ECB's work.
10Y Bund yields are in a 3.32-3.39% range this week and 10Y OAT-Bund spreads remain below 160bp. EUR/USD briefly recovered toward 1.1150 but is back below it. Italy sells €7.75bn of supply today.

The UK Budget cleared the immediate hurdle for Gilts, but Mizuho stops short of calling it structurally bullish. £15bn of headroom avoided a fiscal-stress scenario, the remit was as expected, and reduced long-end issuance gave technical support. The curve flattened and long-end Gilts richened slightly on ASW.

The Budget pushes the problem out. Borrowing is worse than the March OBR path, 2027 growth was revised materially lower and tougher spending choices were deferred. Mizuho sees 2027 as the real test, since higher interest costs or weaker tax receipts would quickly erode the cushion. GBP/USD is consolidating around 1.3325.

Asian sentiment soured after weak tech earnings. JGBs continued to bear-steepen, with the front end anchored by a strong 2Y JGB auction while long-end selling continued. USD/JPY fell below 158 after testing 158.25 before the FOMC. DXY is around 102.25 after falling post-FOMC.
